result.title: Stepwise Reasoning Verification: Don't Generate, Classify!
result.summary: Verifying the reasoning of large language models is increasingly important as they are applied to complex mathematical and scientific problems. Existing work focuses on large decoder models and reports mixed results for generative and discriminative verifiers, leaving unclear which paradigm is more effective and whether large models are necessary. In this work, we cast stepwise verification as a natural language inference task: the problem and partial solution prefix form the premise, while the next reasoning step serves as the hypothesis to be classified as entailed or non-entailed. This formulation enables error localisation at individual reasoning steps and direct comparison of encoder classification, decoder classification, and decoder verdict generation across model scales and annotation budgets. Across five reasoning datasets, a 0.15B encoder classifier outperforms most generative verifiers with up to 4B parameters. On identical decoder backbones, classification outperforms generation from 0.5B to 4B parameters and matches it on the strongest 7B backbone---reaching comparable performance with roughly one tenth as many annotated problems. Our findings establish classification as a parameter- and data-efficient approach to stepwise verification and show that strong verification does not require large generative decoders.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作把步骤级推理验证重构为自然语言推理任务，以问题加部分解答前缀为前提、下一步推理为待分类假设，在五个推理数据集上比较编码器分类、解码器分类与解码器生成式判定，发现 0.15B 编码器分类器优于多数至 4B 的生成式验证器，且分类范式更省参数与标注。
AI.relevance_reason: 步骤级判别式验证器可能为 LVR 的推理链／latent 轨迹校验与停止、回退判据提供低成本组件线索；但该研究为纯文本设定，其对多模态内部状态是否适用尚待核查。
